verdict.root_cause: A traffic-shaping container was attached to cartservice's network namespace by platform-automation at 09:27:37, ~3 minutes before onset, applying a fixed 300ms zero-jitter delay on eth0 with no removal recorded [tr_041e8eababa9]. Every network round-trip out of cartservice pays that toll, so Redis HGET/HMSET spans run ~300-311ms and handlers cost whole multiples of the quantum (GetCart/EmptyCart ~301-307ms, AddItem ~602-613ms), with the gRPC server span exceeding its Redis children by only 1-2ms [tr_4df94ae95359]. The same quantum appears on the caller side of cartservice calls. cartservice itself stays up and error-free through 09:33 [tr_b943808dbafa]; it is waiting, not failing. The multi-second waits propagate to frontend (~1512-1568ms cart POSTs, ~2466-2476ms PlaceOrder) and produce checkoutservice's new error ratio against a flat-zero baseline [tr_7cd7dc5bfb69], explaining the 15-second-later alerts.
verdict.reasoning: The change record and the trace shape converge independently: an injected 300ms fixed delay predicts exactly the near-constant, per-operation, non-proportional quantum the traces show, which organic load, GC, CPU or payload growth would not produce [tr_041e8eababa9][tr_4df94ae95359]. Traces exclude a mesh-wide injection (non-cartservice hops stay under ~25ms) and in-handler compute (server span barely exceeds its children). Clean cartservice logs with continuous traffic [tr_b943808dbafa] fit a service that waits rather than errors, with the failure surfacing at callers [tr_7cd7dc5bfb69]. Class is dependency_latency because the mechanism now breaking requests is waiting on slow cache round-trips; the netem attachment is the act. Fix is detaching the shaping container/clearing the qdisc - not a rollback (hotfix image was already reverted ~14m before onset) and not a restart, since the delay lives on the namespace interface.
open_questions: checkoutservice errors first cross threshold at 07:16, again at 07:44 and 09:10, all before the netem attachment [tr_7cd7dc5bfb69]; nothing dispatched tied those to the earlier automation churn, so 09:31 may be the latest episode of a repeating pattern.

No cartservice latency or request-rate metric exists at all - the series is absent in both windows [tr_6cdb3155df5c] - so the 300ms step rests on traces alone and there is no confirmation the delay is still active.
The error mechanism at checkoutservice (deadline exceeded vs. something else) was never read from its logs or timeout config.

alternatives.root_cause: The earlier REDIS_ADDR port override or hotfix image left cartservice degraded and the 09:31 alert is a continuation.
alternatives.why_not: Both were reverted 1.7h and 14m before onset [tr_041e8eababa9], and the 300ms-quantum trace signature matches netem, not a wrong endpoint.

alternatives.root_cause: redis-cart itself became slow, and cartservice is merely the caller that waited.
alternatives.why_not: The identical ~300ms quantum also appears on the client side of inbound cartservice calls from frontend and checkoutservice [tr_4df94ae95359], which a slow Redis backend cannot explain; a namespace-level delay can.

proposal.expected_effect: Recreating cartservice from its recorded prior configuration gives it a fresh network namespace, dropping the 300ms eth0 delay attached at 09:27:37. In Jaeger: Redis HGET/HMSET spans fall from ~300-311ms to single-digit ms, GetCart/EmptyCart from ~301-307ms and AddItem from ~602-613ms to low ms, frontend cart POSTs from ~1512-1568ms and PlaceOrder from ~2466-2476ms to sub-100ms. checkoutservice error ratio should return toward its flat-zero baseline.
proposal.if_wrong: If new cartservice traces still show the ~300ms per-Redis-op quantum after the recreate, the shaping survived container recreation (or is applied outside the namespace) and this action did not address it. If spans go fast but checkoutservice errors persist, the error mechanism is not latency-driven - consistent with the unexplained 07:16/07:44/09:10 crossings that predate the netem attachment. Note cartservice has no latency or request-rate metric series at all, so confirmation rests on traces and checkoutservice's error ratio only.
proposal.risk: If the diagnosis is wrong, this is a needless container recreate: cartservice drops in-flight requests and its in-process cache, briefly raising checkoutservice/frontend errors, and the reverted prior config may itself be stale (the change log shows repeated automation churn including a REDIS_ADDR edit). Worse, platform-automation has reattached the shaper before (attach ~2.0h before onset, then removal), so it may reattach after the revert, hiding the fix or re-breaking the service.
proposal.blast_radius: cartservice, and its inbound callers during the recreate: frontend and checkoutservice see resets or failed cart calls for a few seconds; loadgenerator sees this as user-facing errors.

triage_judgement.reasoning: Multiple services alerted within seconds along the cart/checkout/frontend path, which is a coherent failure pattern rather than a single isolated warning. No open incident covers it, so it warrants investigation with a shared upstream dependency as the cheap first guess.
